title: Compact Performance Canvas for Model & Route — Chart Spec and Prototype
creator: Samira Patel
description: Design a compact, multi-resolution performance canvas for the Redwood Console that presents per-model and per-route metrics (latency, throughput, token counts) in a single horizontal space-optimized view. The canvas is intended for engineers and SREs to rapidly compare model variants and routes, identify regressions, and correlate rollouts/changes with metric shifts. This ticket includes high-fidelity chart specs, interaction patterns, accessibility considerations, and a clickable prototype for user testing.
acceptance_criteria: Compact canvas displays latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) as overlaid lines with configurable time ranges (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d)
Throughput rendered as area chart behind percentiles with normalized units (requests/s) and optional smoothing toggle
Token usage shown as stacked histogram aligned to the same time axis and grouped by route or model variant
Timebrush + zoom: users can select a region in the overview to drill into a focused chart area while preserving context
Annotations track rollout events (canary start, full rollout, fallback) with markers and an expandable timeline panel
Chart color palette adheres to Redwood brand accessibility standards (WCAG AA contrast) and remains consistent across console pages
Prototype linked and usability-tested with at least 3 platform engineers with documented feedback
design_notes: Primary goal: surface regressions fast — prioritize clarity of percentile separations over visual complexity
Use a multilayer chart: throughput area (low opacity), latency lines (distinct stroke widths), token histogram (stacked bars) — all sharing x-axis time
Introduce a compact legend with toggles to hide/show series; hovering should highlight a single series across charts
Implement sampling rules: for >1M points, show adaptive downsampling and indicate sampling in tooltip
Provide an 'Compare by' control: route | model | variant | region — switches grouping for stacked token bars and series breakdown
Include a lightweight anomaly band visualization (semi-opaque range) for historical alert thresholds
Mobile: collapse histogram and show a single combined metric to keep the view readable on narrow widths
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Lee): prefer arranging tokens on secondary axis rather than stacked overlay to reduce visual confusion — suggested a toggle for stacked vs secondary-axis
ENG (Priya Nair): request for explicit guidance on downsampling algorithm and how it interacts with SLO calculation; flagged potential backend metric parity issues
SRE (Marco Alvarez): asked for clearer annotation handling when multiple rollouts overlap; recommended collapsible event list for the timeline
Accessibility (R&D): color palette passes AA for primary lines but suggested thicker strokes for P99 at small sizes and keyboard focus states for the timebrush
decisions: Adopt overlaid percentile lines + throughput area as default; provide 'split view' toggle that places throughput in a stacked panel below for users who need separate scaling
Implement downsampling using max-min sampling per bucket to preserve spikes; include 'raw' toggle for exact values when time span < 1 hour
Rollout events will be modeled as first-class timeline annotations with short IDs linking to rollout details page
Charting library: prototype assumes Plotly-like canvas for performance, but final implementation to evaluate React + WebGL layer (PixiJS/DeckGL) for large-series rendering
tasks: Handoff: export Figma tokens and CSS variables for chart colors and typography
Spec: finalize detailed tooltip spec including comparisons across routes and absolute vs relative diffs
Dev: spike for rendering 10k datapoints with WebGL prototype — ENG support required
Usability: schedule 3 sessions with backend and platform engineers; collect subjective clarity ratings
Docs: create a console help doc describing chart interactions and the meaning of percentile lines
